data.narrative:
Addionics is a Series B climate and energy technology company that has raised $39M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (KoBold Metals at $3.0B Series C, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B Series C, and Amogy at $700M Series C), alongside one public comparable and eight additional private reference points in the broader climate tech landscape.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $39M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage step-ups, yields $74M. Peer-median analysis across the three same-sector comparables produces a $1.0B median valuation, with a range of $700M to $3.0B. The wide peer range reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity and capital intensity within climate energy.

Synthesizing both methods produces a triangulated range of $63M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $537M. The low end anchors to stage-progression mechanics; the high end reflects peer medians. Key uncertainties include Addionics' relative position within the peer cohort on technology readiness, path to unit economics, and addressable market capture relative to the three comparables used. The wide range ($63M–$1.1B) signals meaningful sensitivity to assumptions about development stage and competitive positioning.
